prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t responsibly name one single “best” lawyer — that depends on the facts of your crash, the injuries, your goals (quick settlement vs trial), and how you want to work with an attorney. I can, however, tell you how to find the best personal injury/car-accident lawyer in Columbus and help you evaluate candidates.

Quick plan
- Decide what you want: trial-ready attorney vs negotiator who settles quickly.  
- Search for local, experienced car-accident personal injury lawyers.  
- Interview 2–4 attorneys and compare answers on the items below.  
- Hire whoever has the best combination of experience, communication, and fee terms you’re comfortable with.

Where to look
- Columbus Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (local vetted referrals).  
- Super Lawyers (Ohio lists top-rated attorneys).  
- Martindale-Hubbell / AV Preeminent ratings.  
- Google / Yelp reviews and recent client testimonials.  
- Ask friends/family or other lawyers for referrals.  
If you want, give your ZIP code and I can produce a short list of well-reviewed Columbus firms to call.

What to check in a lawyer
- Focus and experience with Ohio car-accident and personal injury law.  
- Trial experience (if your case might need litigation).  
- Track record with cases similar to yours (injury type, damages).  
- Clear contingency-fee arrangement and what percent + who advances costs.  
- Communication style and responsiveness (how often you’ll hear updates).  
- Availability and whether the lawyer or a junior handles most work.  
- License standing and any disciplinary history (Ohio Supreme Court public records).  

Important questions to ask in the free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident PI cases in Columbus/Ohio?  
- Have you tried cases against the insurance company/defense counsel I’m likely to face?  
- What similar case results can you share (settlement or verdict) — anonymous totals are fine?  
- What is your contingency fee percentage and what costs will I owe if we don’t recover?  
- How long do you expect this type of case to take?  
- Who will handle day-to-day work and who will I contact?  
- Do you think this should settle or go to trial? Why?

Typical fee matters to expect
- Most PI attorneys work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Common fees: ~33% for negotiation, up to 40% if case goes to trial or appeal (ask specifics).  
- You may also owe case costs (expert fees, medical records, filing fees) that the firm typically advances and is reimbursed from the recovery. Get those details in writing.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or “I’ll get you X” promises.  
- Pressure to sign quickly without time to compare.  
- Poor communication during intake or delays returning calls.  
- No trial experience if your injuries are serious or liability is disputed.

If you want, I can:
- Produce a short list of top-reviewed Columbus personal injury firms (give your ZIP or neighborhood).  
- Draft a short script/email you can use to contact lawyers for consultations.  
- Walk you through evaluating answers after a consultation.

Which would you prefer?
